Library

Our reading list for financial knowledge and intelligence.

EVERYDAY ECONOMICS

Day to Day Economics — Satish Y. Deodhar

An IIM Ahmedabad Business Books Series title — everyday economic ideas explained through everyday situations.

INDIAN CONTEXT

Let's Talk Money — Monika Halan

A practical, India-specific guide to organising personal finances.

GETTING STARTED

Let's Talk Money: Road to Riches Made Easy — Akhil Khanna

A simple, accessible starting point for readers new to organising their money.

BUSINESS

What the CEO Wants You to Know — Ram Charan

How the basic logic of business — cash, margin, growth — really works, in plain terms.

MINDSET

Rich Dad Poor Dad — Robert Kiyosaki

A classic on how assets, liabilities, and mindset shape financial outcomes.

BEHAVIOUR

The Psychology of Money — Morgan Housel

How emotion and behaviour, more than knowledge, drive financial outcomes.

GLOBAL MARKETS

The World for Sale — Javier Blas & Jack Farchy

How commodity traders move money, power, and the earth's resources around the globe.

FUNDAMENTALS

The Intelligent Investor — Benjamin Graham

The value-investing classic on separating price from worth, and staying disciplined.

TIMELESS PRINCIPLES

The Tao of Warren Buffett — Mary Buffett & David Clark

Short, quotable principles behind Buffett's approach to value and patience.

FinFunda

The fundamentals, explained plainly — tap a term to expand it.

SIP

A Systematic Investment Plan invests a fixed amount at regular intervals, buying more units when prices are low and fewer when high — averaging cost over time.

Compounding

Returns earned on your investment start earning their own returns. The longer money stays invested, the more this effect works for you.

Diversification

Spreading money across asset types and funds so that no single loss can derail the whole portfolio.

Risk profile

A structured read of how much volatility you can tolerate, based on your goals, timeline, and temperament.

Emergency fund

3–6 months of expenses kept easily accessible, before other investing begins, so a shock doesn't force you to sell long-term holdings.

LTCG on equity funds

Gains on equity mutual funds held over a year are taxed as long-term capital gains, at rates set by current tax law.
